bib.title: Unified Scaling Laws for Routed Language Models

question: How does validation loss of routed (conditionally-computed) language models scale jointly in dense model size N and expert count E, and can one law cover dense and routed models and several routing techniques?
hypothesis: The converged log-loss of a Routing Network is bilinear in log N and log of a saturating transform of E.
contributions: Routing improves language models across all sizes and variants attempted
RL-based routing (RL-R) is comparably effective to state-of-the-art techniques
Performance of all routing networks is described by scaling laws in N and E that generalize Kaplan et al. 2020
Laws restated in parameter count and inference compute cover more architectures
They imply an Effective Parameter Count equating dense and routed performance

method.summary: Trains a sweep of decoder-only Transformers (15M to 1.3B dense size, 1 to 512 experts, 168 models) with three routing techniques (S-BASE, HASH, RL-R) on a fixed 130B-token budget, fits a bilinear-with-saturation law in (N, E) to final validation loss, then derives Effective Parameter Count and compares techniques via fitted coefficients.
method.task: autoregressive language modelling; scaling-law fitting of validation NLL

datasets.name: multi-trillion-token English compendium (web + open-source text; details in Rae et al. 2021, Gopher)
datasets.size: 130 billion tokens seen per run (multi-trillion available)
datasets.split: validation set whose statistics match training distribution

datasets.name: LAMBADA, The Pile, Curation Corpus, WikiText-103, C4

models.name: Dense Transformer sizes 15M,25M,55M,130M,370M,870M,1.3B
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer (GPT-2 style, relative positional encodings Dai 2019); dff=4*dmodel

models.name: S-BASE, RL-R (RLR-B), HASH routed Transformers
models.architecture: every other FFW replaced by E experts, E in 2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512; K=1 default; capacity factor C=2

other.7B RL-R model: dmodel 4096, 32 layers, 32 heads, E=64, K/V 128, batch 1024, 100k steps, PG weight 1e-1, balancing 1e-1 (App G)

training.objective: next-token NLL; S-BASE adds load-balancing loss; RL-R adds policy-gradient (REINFORCE with learned baseline, Huber value loss, entropy reg) plus balancing loss
training.precision: params bfloat16, optimizer stats float32, softmax ops (attention, router) upcast to float32
training.regularisation: load-balancing aux loss weight 1 (RL-R), S-BASE robust over 1e-3 to 1; Sinkhorn etol 1e-2
training.hardware: TPUs, JAX; data + expert + sharding parallelism; 4 or 8 local experts per device
training.seeds: 3 seeds only for 130M, 8 and 256 experts + dense, 100,000 steps; main sweep single seed

other.RL-R hyperparameters (RLR-B, Table 5): policy entropy weight -5e-4; load balancing 1; policy gradient 1e-2; nucleus top-p 1.; value weight 1e-2; value hidden layers 1 (size dmodel/8); Huber
other.token dropping: capacity C=2 in training; evaluation allows all tokens

inference.samples: single run per config; eval is validation loss

metrics.name: validation loss
metrics.definition: negative log-likelihood on held-out data matching training distribution, final (best) value treated as converged

metrics.name: leave-one-out RMSLE of fit
metrics.definition: held-out error of log-log scaling-law prediction

eval.protocol: fit scaling law to 168 models; leave-one-out prediction error; seed noise 0.01 (cut-off 0.02 for significance)

evidence.quote: The learning rate starts at 1e-7 and decays to 2e-5 with a cosine decay rate over the entire

results.claim: Equation (1) fits all three routing methods on a sweep of six model sizes and nine expert counts
results.setup: Sweep over dense N and E in 2..512, three techniques, 130B tokens
results.quote: This totals 168 different models, including dense baselines.

results.claim: Dense scaling exponent re-estimated close to Kaplan
Bilinear+saturation fit leave-one-out RMSLE for S-BASE
results.table: Table 1, row Bilin. + saturat. in (N, E), column S-BASE

results.claim: Fitted interaction coefficient c for S-BASE is lowest among techniques (best scaling)
Fitted Emax for S-BASE (saturation of expert scaling)
A 5M model with 128 experts matches a 55M dense model that needs over ten times more compute per inference
results.quote: a model with N = 5M and E = 128 equals the performance of a model with N = 55M and E = 1

results.claim: Routing stops helping above Ncutoff; values for S-BASE, RL-R, HASH
results.setup: Extrapolation of Eq. (1) at 130B tokens; highly dependent on token count and on b to second decimal
results.quote: Ncutoff equals 937B, 85B and 83B for S-BASE, RL-R and HASH respectively.

results.claim: Practitioner recommendation: use routing for any model with N up to 1.3B
results.quote: Use routing when training any model with N ⩽1.3B.
with different seeds diverging by no more than 0.01 before 100, 000 steps

results.claim: Training the 15M dense model 4x longer still reduces loss, so models are not converged at 130B tokens
results.quote: training for 4x longer further reduces the validation loss by 0.05
the same model with E = 512 gets a 0.07 reduction in loss from 4x more tokens
end-to-end model overhead of 1% to 3% compared to Switch

results.claim: K=1 is always on the FLOP-efficiency Pareto front
results.quote: K = 1 is always in the pareto front

results.claim: Downstream EPC differs by task for the same routed model (validation 370M, LAMBADA 284M, Pile 535M)
results.setup: N=110M, E=32, simplified EPC with Estart=1 Emax=inf
results.quote: the EPC validation for N=110M, E=32 is 370M, but EPC lambada for the same model is 284M, while EPC pile is 535M

results.claim: RL-R 7B base model with 64 experts still beats a dense model of same size (anecdotal, different training setup)
results.setup: Batch 1024, 100k steps, evaluated at 100B tokens; one run
results.quote: the routed 7B model substantially outperforms the baseline

limits: All numeric values hold only at 130B tokens; authors show models are unconverged and b depends on position in LR schedule (App F.2).
Ncutoff extremely sensitive to b: error in second decimal shifts it by orders of magnitude (App G).
Only K=1..4, R 0.25..1, single seed for the main sweep; largest dense base 1.3B (one 7B anecdote).
Zero-shot downstream scaling differs per task; no dedicated study.
Disputes Kaplan et al. Eq 1.6 L(N,S); authors do not claim to disprove it.
Routing frequency R=1/L deviates from the law.
